title: The Threat Landscape and Your Role
summary: Who attacks financial firms and why, how attacks usually succeed through people rather than technology, and why every member of staff is part of the firm's defences.
contentGaps: Written as part of a programme: Aim and Purpose is the module's one-line description; audience, prior knowledge and core reading come from the programme

sections.Aim and Purpose: Who attacks financial firms and why, how attacks usually succeed through people rather than technology, and why every member of staff is part of the firm's defences.
Learning Objectives: Explain the main cyber threats and threat actors facing financial firms
Recognise why staff are often both the first target and the first line of defence
Describe the impact of cyber incidents on customers, the firm and the wider system
Syllabus: Threat actors: criminals, insiders, hacktivists and state-linked groups
Ransomware, data theft, fraud and service disruption
How attacks unfold: from first contact to impact
Why supervisors and boards treat cyber and resilience as top risks
Intended Audience: All staff in regulated firms, including new joiners, contractors and temporary staff with access to the firm's systems
Front-office, operations, technology, HR, finance and support staff who handle customer data or critical processes
Line managers responsible for secure working practices and continuity arrangements in their teams
sections.Useful Prior Knowledge and Experience: No technical background is required. The programme is suitable for new joiners and as annual refresher training.
Core Reading: ISO/IEC (2022), ISO/IEC 27001:2022 Information Security, Cybersecurity and Privacy Protection – Information Security Management Systems – Requirements
ISO (2019), ISO 22301:2019 Security and Resilience – Business Continuity Management Systems – Requirements
